attributes.body_ja:
「たて」は、動詞（どうし）「立（た）てる」から生（う）まれた接尾語（せつびご）です。動詞（どうし）の連用形（れんようけい）に付（つ）けて使（つか）われます。「たて」は「(A) をしたばかり」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

「たて」は接尾語（せつびご）なので、動詞（どうし）とつながると名詞（めいし）になります。そのため、「たて」のあとに名詞（めいし）を付（つ）ける場合（ばあい）は、格助詞（かくじょし）の「の」が必要（ひつよう）です。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「たて」は、何（なに）かが終（お）わったという事実（じじつ）そのものではなく、それが終（お）わった「直後（ちょくご）」であることを表（あらわ）す接尾語（せつびご）です。そのため、それが終（お）わった時（とき）から時間（じかん）が経（た）つと質（しつ）が落（お）ちてしまうような、「時間（じかん）」が重視（じゅうし）される物事（ものごと）について使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
たて, coming from the verb 立（た）てる 'to stand' is a suffix in Japanese that is often used after the conjunctive form of verbs. たて conveys that something has 'just been finished', or is 'freshly finished'.

As a suffix, たて transforms verbs into nouns. This means that they may be followed by a (B) phrase, or followed directly by the case marking particle の and a noun.

Fun Fact

たて is a suffix that is used to convey the moment in time directly after something has been finished, rather than the fact that it 'is' finished. Due to this, たて is most frequently used with verbs that indicate some sense of time based importance, where (A) will degrade in quality over time after completion.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: Both express recency but differ in usage. たばかり follows た-form verbs to show something just happened, e.g. 焼いたばかり 'just baked'. たて attaches to stems and means 'freshly done', e.g. 焼きたてのパン 'freshly-baked bread'.

Both かけ and たて describe transitional states of actions, but with opposite timing. かけ refers to something that is incomplete or in progress, often implying interrupted action, e.g. 食べかけのパン 'half-eaten bread'. たて, by contrast, refers to something freshly completed, emphasizing newness and immediacy, e.g. 焼きたてのパン 'freshly baked bread'.

first_relatable.meaning: Half-, Not yet finished, About to, Begin to

attributes.body: たところだ and たて are similar in that both refer to something that has just happened, but they differ in usage and nuance. たところだ uses the past tense of a verb and simply describes the timing, e.g. パンを焼いたところだ ('I just baked some bread.'). In contrast, たて attaches to verb stems and has the nuance of 'freshly done/finished', e.g. 焼きたてのパンが一番美味しい ('Freshly baked bread is the most delicious.').

first_relatable.title: たところだ
first_relatable.meaning: Just finished doing, Was just doing
